official.deadline_note: PSC publishes a single central closing date of 15 March 2027 for the 2027 round and no separate institutional deadline. Note that the application is only counted as complete once the form, the essay and all supporting documents are uploaded and submitted, so an unfinished upload on 15 March 2027 effectively misses the deadline.

Psychometric Assessments assessing general, verbal and numerical reasoning abilities

coverage: Tuition fees and other approved charges
For overseas degrees, return airfare will be provided
A series of sponsored development programmes, including student exchange and summer opportunities
application_method: Step 1 - Prepare supporting documents before filling in the application form
Step 2 - Log in via Singpass at pscgateway.gov.sg to access the application form
Step 3a - Submit the application form (Personal & Family Details, Education History, Achievements, Career and Course Preferences, University Applications, Other Details, Declaration) and an essay
Step 3b - Upload and submit all supporting documents
Step 3c - Receive a video interview link within 7 days of submission and complete the video interview
Step 4 - Receive application outcome by June; shortlisted candidates proceed to assessments and a panel interview
official.application_route: Apply online through the PSC Gateway (Singpass login) and complete the application form, essay, supporting document uploads and a video interview; shortlisted candidates then undergo psychometric, game-based and psychological assessments before a PSSB panel interview.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be Singapore Citizens. No separate residency rule is published.
official.international_eligibility: International students are not eligible - the official eligibility criteria require applicants to be Singapore Citizens.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Courses must be relevant to the Public Service and are subject to PSC's approval; MBA programmes are not allowed. PSC Master's Scholarship (Sustainability) applicants should intend to read a Master's in a field related to sustainability and circularity.
official.duration: Any country of study; maximum 2 years of study; 3-year bond.
official.description: The PSC Master's Scholarships are the premier merit-based government scholarships for those who wish to pursue a Master's degree and a career in Public Administration in the Singapore Public Service. Applicants choose between the PSC Master's Scholarship and the PSC Master's Scholarship (Sustainability), with the Sustainability variant developing a perspective in sustainability and circularity and a first posting in a related role. Holders study for a maximum of two years in any country, serve a three-year bond, and are emplaced on the Public Service Leadership Programme on graduation.
official.program_type: Government postgraduate scholarship for the Singapore Public Service, Public Administration track

applicant_utility.summary: The PSC Master's Scholarship is a Singapore Public Service leadership pipeline award rather than a study grant: you apply once through the Singpass-gated PSC Gateway and the funding follows your approved Master's, so the course you name has to clear PSC first and an MBA is excluded outright. The 15 March 2027 closing date is firm for the 2027 intake and the window opens on 1 September 2026, giving you roughly six and a half months to build a genuinely competitive record rather than just to fill in a form. PSC publishes no stipend, allowance or tuition figure at all, so you cannot budget from the website - budget on the basis that tuition, approved charges, return airfare for overseas study and maintenance allowances are covered, and confirm the actual allowance quantum with PSC before you commit to an expensive overseas programme. Treat the three-year bond, the post-graduation Public Service Leadership Programme placement and the start-in-the-next-academic-year condition as core terms of the deal, not footnotes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year Singapore Citizen undergraduates, and fresh graduates with at most three years of private or non-government sector experience, who want a policy and leadership career in the Singapore Public Service and a PSC-approved Master's outside MBA disciplines.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your Singpass works well before 1 September 2026 and use a laptop or desktop - the PSC portal has not supported mobile devices or tablets since 21 December 2023.
Retrieve Secondary 4/Year 4 year-end school reports including teachers' comments and your CCA and CIP records now; these are the items applicants most often cannot reconstruct late.
Assemble university transcripts and university CCA records, plus employment, NS and Public Service internship testimonials where applicable.

Decide early between the standard and the Sustainability variant, because the Sustainability route requires a Master's in a sustainability-and-circularity-related field and fixes your first posting to that area.
Raise course approval informally with PSC before you name your Master's, since courses must be relevant to the Public Service and are subject to PSC approval.
Write the essay in parallel with the application form rather than after it - the application only counts as complete when the form, essay and all uploads are all submitted.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the form but leaving the essay or some supporting documents unfinished - PSC explicitly states the application is only complete when all three parts are in.
Naming an MBA, or a course PSC judges not relevant to the Public Service, which fails the approval condition outright.
Missing the Singapore Citizenship bar, or exceeding the three-year working-experience cap, which counts only private or non-government sector work and includes part-time and contract roles.
Applying when you cannot realistically start the Master's in the academic year immediately following the offer - deferral is not offered.
Ignoring or delaying the video interview link, which arrives within 7 days of submission and leaves a short window to respond.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: PSC publishes no allowance amounts, so the uncovered figure cannot be verified from official sources. In practice applicants should still fund pre-departure and relocation costs, visa and medical costs for overseas study, family or dependant costs, and any charge PSC does not classify as 'approved', alongside the opportunity cost of the three-year bond.
document_audit: Preliminary examination results are explicitly not required - do not pad the upload with them in place of the actual qualification certificates.
Employment testimonials are marked 'if applicable', but a candidate with private-sector experience who omits them looks incomplete.
For male Singaporean applicants the NS Certificate of Service and Testimonial is a separate document from employment testimonials and is frequently the last item located.
University results are entered per semester as required form fields, so collect every semester's record rather than a single consolidated transcript.
The portal requires NRIC and family member particulars as form fields, so have those to hand before starting rather than discovering the gap mid-upload.
alerts: Applications for the 2027 round close on 15 March 2027; the window runs 1 September 2026 to 15 March 2027 and the video interview link follows within 7 days of submission.
The application portal has not supported mobile devices or tablets since 21 December 2023 - plan to submit from a desktop.
You must be able to start the Master's in the academic year immediately after the offer; you cannot defer the intake.

A three-year bond follows a maximum of two years of study, holders are emplaced on the Public Service Leadership Programme on graduation, and Sustainability variant holders take a first posting in a sustainability and circularity role.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Singpass-gated PSC Gateway form, essay and document uploads; a video interview link follows within about 7 days, and only shortlisted candidates progress to psychometric, game-based and psychological assessments before a PSSB panel interview, with outcomes communicated by June.
